breaking.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse with no deal as EU rejects fossil-fuel-free draft
breaking.fact: The U.N. climate summit in Antalya collapsed Sunday after the EU and others rejected a final draft that never mentioned fossil fuels — the first COP to end with no deal since Copenhagen in 2009. COP31 president Murat Kurum conceded there was no consensus and the text would not be adopted, after the summit ran a record 44 hours past its scheduled close.

breaking.headline: FBI investigating hack of its national crime database
breaking.fact: Hackers breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center, the database police nationwide use to check warrants, missing persons and stolen property; the FBI is investigating what was taken or altered. President Trump confirmed the breach in a Saturday Fox News interview, calling it 'not good' — the bureau's second cyberattack in months, after a September breach of its jobs portal.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump seeks a 'permanent' Iran deal; next move may wait until 2027
weekInBrief.body: President Trump told an Israeli outlet and Fox News he wants a permanent agreement barring Iran from ever getting a nuclear weapon and is in no rush, saying a decision on next steps could wait until 2027. CBS reports the U.S. and Israel are weighing another military assault, while the Senate narrowly rejected a war-powers measure to pull U.S. forces out of the conflict.

weekInBrief.headline: Schumer faces a leadership challenge after Democrats' Senate sweep
weekInBrief.body: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader in the first contested race since 1994, arguing the party needs new leadership after flipping nine seats for a 56-seat majority. Schumer, who turns 76 on Monday, says he will be elected majority leader in the Dec. 1 secret vote; at least 16 Democrats back him, six back Van Hollen.

weekInBrief.headline: Medicare open enrollment runs through Dec. 7
weekInBrief.body: Annual open enrollment for Medicare — covering about 70 million people — runs through Dec. 7, with choices taking effect Jan. 1. CMS set the 2027 standard Part B premium at $209.40 a month, up $6.50, and the Part D out-of-pocket cap rises to $2,400. Some Medicare Advantage plans are ending in certain markets, so checking your plan's status is worth the time.

weekInBrief.headline: AAA: 81.5 million Americans to travel for Thanksgiving
weekInBrief.body: AAA projects 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home over the Nov. 24–30 Thanksgiving period — down 0.1% from last year, ending a three-year streak of records, with volumes near record levels anyway. About 72.9 million will drive and 5.96 million will fly; the heaviest road congestion is expected Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons.

weekendStories.headline: Lone Star College gives away 300 free Thanksgiving meal bundles
weekendStories.body: Lone Star College–North Harris handed out free Thanksgiving meal bundles — a turkey and the side dishes — to the first 300 families on Saturday, Nov. 21, no registration required. Now in its second year, the drive is hosted by trustee Daniel Meza with faculty, staff and student volunteers pitching in.

weekendStories.headline: Houston Food Bank opens its 46th holiday phone bank
weekendStories.body: The Houston Food Bank, the nation's largest food bank, is recruiting volunteers 16 and older for its 46th Share Your Holidays phone bank, Nov. 30 to Dec. 4 at its Portwall Street headquarters. Callers will reserve special holiday food boxes for neighbors facing food insecurity, with bilingual Spanish-speaking volunteers especially needed.

weekendStories.headline: Plains Trotters reach the state volleyball tournament for the first time in 27 years
weekendStories.body: Plains residents packed the high school gym for a send-off pep rally as the Trotters volleyball team headed to the state tournament in Bozeman — the program's first trip to state in 27 years. The team, coached by Kim Lakko, earned its berth with a tough divisional run, and the whole town turned out to cheer them on.

weekendStories.headline: Orphaned mountain lion cub finds a best friend for life
weekendStories.body: A 6-week-old mountain lion cub, found abandoned and freezing near Fort Belknap, was rescued by a volunteer who braved early winter storms to carry her to the Yellowstone Wildlife Sanctuary. Now named Nakoda — 'friend' in the Nakoda language — she has been paired at Buttonwood Park Zoo with Cascade, another orphaned cub, and the two have bonded beautifully.

weekendStories.headline: Governor pardons turkey Alice, and 54 turkeys go to families in need
weekendStories.body: Gov. Kelly Armstrong pardoned a turkey named Alice at the North Dakota Capitol on Monday, keeping the state's annual Thanksgiving tradition alive. The North Dakota Turkey Federation paired the ceremony with a donation of 54 frozen turkeys to three Bismarck charities feeding families through the holidays.

weekendStories.headline: UND's Community Thanksgiving draws more than 600 for a free meal
weekendStories.body: The University of North Dakota's second annual Community Thanksgiving brought just over 600 students and community members together in the Memorial Union Ballroom for a free holiday meal — up more than 200 guests from last year. Hosted by the Hilyard International Center, the International Center and UND Athletics, the evening also collected thank-you cards for service members.

weekendStories.headline: Marquette County's new bike park is ahead of schedule and under budget
weekendStories.body: The 906 Adventure Team's Gluski Park, a new bike park for riders, walkers and community events in Marquette County, is ahead of schedule and under budget, with the full $1.6 million cost already raised. The park should open next summer, and extra donations mean the whole complex is on track to be debt-free by 2030.

weekendStories.headline: Rhode Island SPCA's first Petsgiving feeds more than 200 families
weekendStories.body: The Rhode Island SPCA held its first-ever Petsgiving drive-thru in Warwick on Saturday, handing out pet food to at least 200 families so pets can stay in their homes through the holidays. A $10,000 Rhode Island Foundation grant stocked the pantry, and organizers framed the day as keeping animals with the families who already love them.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A tanker sailing outbound through the strait was struck by an unidentified projectile Friday about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, catching fire with no casualties reported, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations (Warning 214-26); Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the vessel hit a naval mine, a claim not independently verified. Iran has also positioned more than 14 tankers at Kharg Island in a convoy to test the U.S. blockade, with crews assigned and flags raised, according to TankerTrackers and satellite imagery, while U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Thursday that energy flows through the strait were increasing. On oil, the roughly 200,000 barrels transferred Tuesday has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil and products kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Earth gains a tiny temporary second moon
space.body: A 2-meter asteroid discovered in August, designated 2026 QQ8, has been captured by Earth's gravity and is looping around us as a 'mini moon,' the Minor Planet Center confirmed Oct. 29. Follow-up observations from Arizona and Hawaii confirmed it is a natural object, not debris; it is expected to drift away in early December, and it poses no collision risk.

space.headline: NASA spins Mars helicopter blades past the speed of sound
space.body: NASA engineers pushed experimental Mars helicopter rotor blades beyond the speed of sound in March tests at JPL without breaking them, boosting potential lift by about 30%. The breakthrough could let next-generation helicopters carry heavier science gear and reach terrain rovers cannot, building on Ingenuity's run.

space.headline: Atomic clocks could catch time flowing at two speeds at once
space.body: Physicists at Kyushu University and collaborators in the U.S., Canada and Sweden have worked out how trapped-ion atomic clocks could detect a quantum effect in which a single clock experiences multiple flows of time simultaneously. Published in Physical Review Letters, the method would boost sensitivity 100- to 1,000-fold; turning the theory into an experiment is the next step.

space.headline: Moon dust 3D-printed into LEGO-like bricks for future bases
space.body: University of Arkansas researchers have 3D-printed simulated lunar regolith into interlocking, LEGO-like bricks using laser sintering — no binder needed — a first that could let astronauts build shelters from the dust underfoot. The blocks are still porous and weaker than binder-based versions, so load-bearing use is a way off, but the work was published in npj Advanced Manufacturing.

apod.title: Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno
apod.credit: NASA, Juno spacecraft — Astronomy Picture of the Day
apod.explanation: What colors Jupiter's clouds is still not fully understood — the atmosphere is mostly colorless hydrogen and helium, and trace molecules such as ammonium hydrosulfide are leading candidates. This color-enhanced view from NASA's Juno spacecraft, taken during its 14th low pass in 2018, shows light clouds swirling around reddish regions; lighter clouds generally ride higher than darker ones.

aiModels.notes: The deep-think option from the project's Nov 20 checkpoint: strongest US-open agentic benchmarks and up-to-1M context, but ~80GB and a Linux/WSL2 serving path.
The turnkey option: maker-documented Ollama path, Apache 2.0, fast on mini hardware (~60 tok/s class) — but 128K context sits exactly at the project floor, and it is text-only.

aiHardware.notes: The frontrunner — the only box ticking every project criterion today: CUDA, Windows-native, Microsoft support, shipping now. Bolt-class models run ~84 tok/s on this silicon. Ceiling: 128GB is learning-class; it cannot touch Spark Open itself.
Most memory in a mini — room for the 120B deep-think brain plus a fat 256K KV cache. No CUDA (ROCm/Vulkan serving), you assemble it yourself, and batches sell out.
Cheapest US-company route to a 128GB Windows box. The shortage in one row: launched at $1,999 in Jul 2025, now $4,700 — and Windows caps its GPU memory at 96GB.

The experience today: about half the capability of hosted Muse — chat at full speed, deep thinking at about half pace. A strong junior on the desk, not a replica.
